- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior 5-day high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 10-day horizon to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment is flat or negative (≤0.2) and price is near 30-day mean, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion trap.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to reflect it; adjust downward by 1–2% if sentiment <0.3 and price >30-day MA.
- If sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.4→0.7) and model forecast is flat, it often underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment unit increase.
